summary: The machine under load while lines are typed at its console: every line read and no disk request quarantined; the scenario is machine/load_scenario.c and the probe tests/loadprobe.c

cases.behavior: six spinners, two writers syncing a FAT32 volume on a disk behind the lag device, a pinger and a console reader run at once; the reader takes every line typed and no request is quarantined by its deadline

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the test image with the copy of the disk to the debug shell
run loadprobe at the debug shell, type six lines, each once the reader says it took the one before, take the report from the console and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the FAT32 volume of /dev/disk0p1 mounts on /lo
the report pipe and the ten load processes are made
every load process ends by the kill, and none exits by itself
/proc/stat has the longest delays of the timer, the disk and the console
the reader takes each of the six lines typed at the console
/proc/disk counts no request quarantined by its deadline under the load
the volume unmounts and /lo is removed

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

timing.assumes: rach2.blocklag=1 holds each request of the disk a hundredth of a second before its answer, and the case judges only that no request was quarantined after it; the disk keeps the guest's flushes from the host, so that the host's disk adds nothing to the deadline

native.reason: the case types lines at the console of the machine under load; tests/native/probes.cases runs the probe with its lines on a pseudo-terminal

cases.behavior: the first writer alone, without its syncs, and the console reader, on a disk the ATA driver reads and writes on its data port with interrupts off; the writer gives way at each tick, so that the reader takes every line

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure
